target_customer: Mining companies that buy discovered deposits or exploration targets, and later critical metals offtakers
problem: Mineral exploration has a very low discovery success rate and is slow and costly, so new metal deposits are found rarely.
business_model: Explore with AI and own drilling, then sell or partner discovered deposit rights to larger miners
product_category: AI driven mineral exploration and drilling

founders.name: Roman Teslyuk
education: Ivan Franko University, Ukraine, master's in geology
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2019 calls him a geoscientist with eight years of exploration and academic experience. Another profile says he built the first platform with web designer friend Igor Gerechko, who is not named as a co-founder by the YC page.

competitors.name: GoldSpot Discoveries
competitors.what: Machine learning driven mineral exploration targeting for mining companies

competitors.name: KoBold Metals
competitors.what: AI mineral exploration for battery metals, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, mentioned as part of the same field
competitors.funding_then: Andreessen Horowitz backed, amount not stated

technical_complexity.rationale: Combines geoscience data modelling with later custom low disturbance drilling hardware. Predicting deposits from sparse geological data is hard and validation needs physical drilling.

defensibility.rationale: Discovered deposits and drill data accumulate and proprietary rigs cut cost, but ML targeting was being copied by KoBold and GoldSpot and mining rights are tied to licences.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large miners kept buying services and projects rather than copying; no acquisition of Earth AI found. KoBold went on to raise far larger rounds.

market_need_then: Exploration success rates were low and the company claimed a 50X better success rate in 2018 field tests at about $11,000 per prospect discovery, plus more than 60 mining firms on trial and paid contracts per a profile. Demand for critical metals grew with electrification.

branding.domain_note: Uses earth-ai.com with a hyphen, not earthai.com (source: company site URL).
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage from TechCrunch, The Economist and Mining.com mostly about results, not the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with other Earth AI products, but credible trade and tech press coverage; no sourced brand assets.

pivots.from: Online platform predicting deposits for customers to explore
pivots.to: Predictive explorer and driller owning exploration and low disturbance drilling
pivots.why: Not stated by a source; the YC page and later press describe the vertical integration.

outcome_analysis: Earth AI raised small seed rounds and up to $2.5M from Gagarin Capital around YC, then a $20M Series B in January 2025 led by Tamarack Global and Cantos, helped by the critical metals tailwind. The founder is a geoscientist with a PhD track, fitting the domain. It is still active and building its own labs per April 2026 press, so the outcome is still open.
notes: Series B 2025 reported by Global Mining Review, Axios (via YC page headline), Pulse 2.0 and others, consistent. Seedtable aggregator lists seeds of $600K in 2017 and $1.1M in 2018 and about $9.7M total, unverified and not recorded. Possible Series A of A$20M seen in one undated report, unverified. Total raised per aggregator exceeds recorded rounds, so coverage is partial. The 2019 round is labelled other because the article does not give a stage. Founding year 2016 per YC, other sources say 2017. The 2025 Series B was also stated on the YC page headlines and company profile outlets.
